subject: SIG evidence: requests for CI / PR gating + key rotation samples
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: Ken Brewer <ken.brewer@assessors.io>, security-ops@finapps.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: follow-up — examples of PR gating and key rotation evidence

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG questionnaire review we need a small set of artifacts demonstrating your Secure SDLC controls focused on: 1) PR-based gating (who approves, signed approvals, automated checks), 2) CI credentials/secrets handling (ephemeral tokens, hashed logs), and 3) KMS key rotation proof (policy and recent rotation summary).

Can you share:
- A redacted PR (diff + approval trail) showing enforcement of CODEOWNERS and at least two approvers for a protected branch
- The CI run log for that PR showing secrets masked and agent identity (timestamped)
- A short KMS rotation summary (date of last rotation, rotation policy reference)

We prefer minimal artifacts (redacted) rather than full repos. If you have a one‑page mapping that states where each control is enforced (line numbers, policies, or link to runbook) that would speed review.

Ken (assessor) and our security ops are cc'd. Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Ruiz
Security Manager, FinApps Inc

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>, Ken Brewer <ken.brewer@assessors.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up — examples of PR gating and key rotation evidence

Elena — thanks, understood. Attaching three small artifacts and a brief mapping document. Quick notes:
- PR (pr-4867-approved-diff.patch): redacted diff for the feature in question; approvals captured by our GitHub protected-branch policy (CODEOWNERS + two approvers). Approvals are shown inline (usernames redacted).
- CI run (ci-run-20250430.log): CI agent output with secrets masked and ephemeral token id (EPH-***). We also include the step that fetches secrets via the credential-fetcher service which exchanges ephemeral creds for a short-lived token.
- KMS rotation (kms-rotation-summary-20250401.pdf): PDF export from our KMS showing rotation on 2025-04-01 and the rotation policy doc id.

Below is a short mapping to the SIG control IDs: 
- SIG/SDLC-PR-01: PR approval enforcement — see pr-4867-approved-diff.patch (approved by two CODEOWNERS entries).
- SIG/SDLC-CI-02: Secrets handling — see ci-run-20250430.log showing masked secrets and result of ephemeral token exchange step.
- SIG/SDLC-KMS-04: Rotation proof — kms-rotation-summary-20250401.pdf and policy ref: KMS-ROT-2024-v2.

If you need any additional log levels (audit trail with UUIDs) let us know — we can pull a limited audit export.

Thanks,
Ava

--
Ava Chen
Manager, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference

From: Ken Brewer <ken.brewer@assessors.io>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up — examples of PR gating and key rotation evidence

Thanks Ava — reviewed the artifacts at a high level. A few clarifying questions before we accept them as evidence:
1) In the PR patch the approval block shows approver handles but not timestamps — can you provide either the approval event timestamps (redacted) or commit hashes that include the merge timestamp?
2) CI run looks good; need to confirm the ephemeral token TTL and the service identity that performed the secret fetch (we need an auditable service account id).
3) For KMS rotation: can you supply the policy ARN or internal id and the last three rotation operations (dates only) rather than a single summary?

If you can drop the three small follow-ups into an audit snippet or send a short confirmation email we should be able to close out SIG/SDLC-CI-02 and SIG/SDLC-KMS-04.

- Ken

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Ken Brewer <ken.brewer@assessors.io>, Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up — examples of PR gating and key rotation evidence

Ken — I can provide the extra audit snippets. Quick answers inline:
- PR approval timestamps: We export approval events from GitHub audit log. See attached small CSV extract (pr-4867-approvals.csv) — I've pasted a couple of redacted rows below for convenience: 
  "pr_id,approver,approved_at_utc"
  "4867,alice@redwood.com,2025-04-30T16:12:32Z"
  "4867,bob@redwood.com,2025-04-30T16:15:05Z"

- CI ephemeral token TTL: 15 minutes (EPH tokens issued by cred-exchange). Service account: svc-ci-fetcher@redwood-prod (we maintain a separate service-account-per-pipeline policy). The ci-run log includes the token id (EPH-1a2b***).

- KMS rotation operations: last three rotations: 2023-04-01, 2024-04-01, 2025-04-01. Policy id: KMS-ROT-2024-v2 (internal ref).

I'll attach the CSV and a one-page mapping doc to the folder you shared. Let me know if you need full audit exports (we'll redact emails and user ids).

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finapps.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: Ken Brewer <ken.brewer@assessors.io>, security-ops@finapps.com
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up — examples of PR gating and key rotation evidence

Marissa — this is perfect, thank you. The CSV extract and the token/service-account names are sufficient for our reviewer to verify the controls. We'll mark SIG/SDLC-PR-01 and SIG/SDLC-KMS-04 as addressed pending the formal uploads to your shared Drive link (the hubspot ticket will also be updated).

Ken — if you need the unredacted audit for a spot check, we can request a timeboxed export via the assessor process (preferred).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Ruiz
Security Manager, FinApps Inc
